glossary.definition: Deep learning is machine learning using neural networks with many layers stacked on top of each other, rather than just one or two. Each extra layer lets the network build on what the previous one learned, similar to how a first layer might notice edges in a photo, the next layer combines edges into shapes, and a later layer combines shapes into "this is a face." That extra depth is what made today's boom in image recognition, speech, and language possible.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly raises an additional $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation
items.summary: OpenAI has reportedly raised an additional $11 billion as part of a funding round that hasn't closed yet but is expected to in the coming weeks. OpenAI has reportedly raised $11 billion so far in a new funding round that values the AI lab at $1.25 trillion. Bloomberg reported on the new funding on Friday, citing sources familiar with the matter. The $11 billion is part of a larger funding round that hasn’t closed yet, according to the outlet.

items.title: All the latest updates on AI data centers
items.summary: Massive new data centers are the physical foundation for tech companies’ hopes and dreams for AI. But the rush to expand warehouses full of energy-hungry servers has also kicked up fights across the world over their impact on power grids, utility bills, nearby communities, and the environment. Data centers were a major bipartisan issue ahead of the 2026 midterms , and voters largely opposed data center expansion at the polls. Tech giants like OpenAI and Amazon are promising to work more closely with local communities and cover their data center energy costs.

items.title: Ripple-65B Preview delivers strong agentic coding results as a fully Apache 2.0 open US model
items.summary: S. models on the TerminalBench 2.1 coding benchmark at a total R&D cost of $32 million. On other benchmarks, however, Ripple falls behind the likewise newly released western open model Inkling 2 Small. AI chip design firm Ricursive Intelligence has trained an open language model. Ripple-65B Preview was pretrained on 12 trillion tokens and, according to the company, achieved a score of 80.52 on the TerminalBench 2.1 coding benchmark, the best result among open US models.

items.title: Hundreds of Artex AI hacking tools found publicly exposed to the web
items.summary: Security researchers found hundreds of servers hosting the penetration testing tool Artex exposed to the internet, allowing anyone access to the hacking tool. Security researchers have discovered hundreds of copies of a Chinese-made AI hacking tool publicly exposed to the internet for anyone to access, potentially allowing outsiders to launch cyberattacks against unsuspecting targets. The hacking software, called Artex, is an open source autonomous penetration testing tool, meaning software that automatically probes computer systems for weaknesses, and it’s been linked to several cyberattacks since its public release in July. As open source software, it’s free for anyone to download and run on their own servers, making it a popular tool for those who cannot access Anthropic or OpenAI’s most advanced cybersecurity AI models for discovering security vulnerabilities.

items.title: Free Chinese AI Models Are Getting Scary Good at Hacking
items.summary: An experiment in which AI models were asked to break into simulated networks showed the hacking skills of DeepSeek and GLM to be not far behind OpenAI’s most advanced cyber model, which isn’t public. Open-weight artificial intelligence models are now almost as capable of hacking into computer networks as the best closed ones, according to new research that heralds a much-anticipated turning point in the cybersecurity landscape. Vals , a company that measures AI capabilities, set out to test how well different AI models could carry out complex, multi-step network instructions on mock corporate networks. “The best frontier models, locked up inside the labs and available only through trusted access programs, are now starting to be matched by open models that anybody can download,” says Nikil Ravi, a researcher at Vals.

items.title: Prompt: AI's next bottleneck is outside the data center
items.summary: AI companies are racing to build data centers, but power shortages, regulatory hurdles and local opposition are slowing expansion.

items.title: Could potential AI clones of GTA VI force a quicker official port?
items.summary: Yesterday, when reporting on emerging efforts to pipe the console version of GTA VI through a PC's DLSS-powered Nvidia GPU , we mentioned in passing that PC players could instead just wait for the AI-assisted decompilation port that will no doubt be coming in short order. Now, a former Rockstar tech director says he thinks that exact threat could cause the developer to work faster on the official PC version of its soon-to-release crime/lifestyle simulator. Obbe Vermeij hasn't worked at Rockstar since 2009 , but in a new interview with Rock Paper Shotgun , he recalled how artists for the PC version of the original top-down Grand Theft Auto were incensed when the console version squashed the game's 256-color textures down to 16 colors for the PS1 release. "So it always has been that sort of awkward relationship between PC and the console," Vermeij said.

items.title: A mole in the White House? Residential proxies are everywhere
items.summary: Residential proxies are often used by bad actors to hide the true source of internet traffic — and now one of them appears to have taken up residence in the White House. The Residential Proxy Observatory , set up by Layer3 Intel to monitor the threat of anonymized network activity, has identified proxy exit activity on one particular network, AS2650, which is registered to the executive office of the US President and operated out of the White House. Residential proxies — so-called because they typically run on home or personal devices — mask the true source of internet traffic by rerouting it to appear to come from a different IP address. While it may be concerning that this is activity to be found in one of the protected workspaces in the US, this is in line with recent research from Infoblox , which found that residential proxies were widespread throughout enterprises.

items.title: Enterprises must take blame for their AI agents’ mistakes, say regulators
items.summary: The UK’s digital watchdogs have warned enterprises that they can’t evade their legal responsibilities by blaming errors on AI agents that they have deployed. “By taking action on behalf of users, such as making purchases and communicating with businesses, these agents could transform how people use digital services, engage with markets and unlock wider innovation,” said the Digital Regulation Cooperation Forum (DRCF), a body comprising the UK’s Competition and Markets Authority (CMA), Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO), and communications regulator Ofcom, in a joint statement . ” The DRCF didn’t pull its punches. ” There is certainly a degree of uncertainty over the legal position of autonomous AI agents.

items.title: I watched a humanoid robot clean my apartment. It felt like a taste of the future.
items.summary: I’m not the sort of person who typically pays for a house cleaner. I’m too frugal, and I kind of enjoy putting on a podcast and going to town on my tub with a Magic Eraser. But when I saw an X post about a new humanoid-robot cleaning service in San Francisco, I immediately signed up for the waitlist. I wanted my apartment to feel like The Jetsons , even if just for an hour.

items.title: Smaller Language Models Could Reshape How Enterprises Deploy AI
items.summary: The push to deploy artificial intelligence across enterprise workflows has largely focused on increasingly capable large language models (LLMs) . These systems generate content, interpret complex instructions, and power applications from customer support to software engineering. Yet as organisations move from experimentation to production, the priority shifts: the fundamental question is no longer just how capable a model is, but how reliably we can evaluate, govern, and control its behaviour. This dynamic is bringing smaller language models (SLMs) to the forefront.

items.title: The Anthropic-Indian IT Partnership Is a Two-Way Bet
items.summary: Anthropic’s S-1 filing spends a long passage on competition. It names model developers such as OpenAI and Google, and first-party application providers. IT services firms do not appear. The passages on partners cite systems integrators (SIs) such as Accenture, Deloitte, KPMG and PwC. None is Indian.
